data.content_ref: inline:The target answers why the air stays warmer at night by naming anthropogenic heat emissions and their persistence after sunset. But for the cross-city half of the question it asserts the nighttime gap scales with population density/anthropogenic heat output, treating higher emissions as the single mechanism that makes the gap larger in some cities. That causal priority is backwards for nocturnal UHI: the dominant, well-supported cross-city modulator of the nighttime temperature gap is urban geometry and surface materials via reduced sky-view factor and thermal mass, which slows radiative cooling and stored-heat release. Anthropogenic heat is a secondary contributor and is often a smaller term than stored solar heat and reduced longwave loss, so it cannot be the single best explanation for why the gap is larger in some cities than in others.
